title: Ways to drive it
standfirst: Dashboard, API, SDK, CLI, MCP, SSH, desktop. A provider can have all seven and still be unusable without a terminal, or have three and be genuinely click-driven.
idea: The surfaces fall into two groups. A control plane creates, stops and configures machines: dashboard, REST or gRPC API, SDKs, CLI, and increasingly an MCP server an AI assistant can call. An execution plane gets inside: SSH, a web terminal, a desktop, a file API.

A dashboard that can create a sandbox is not the same as a product that gives you an agent. Several providers can create a machine with a button and still expect a command to do anything useful with it. Others document a prompt to paste into Claude Code or Cursor as the intended no-code path.

MCP is the newest surface and the easiest to misread. A hosted MCP server that manages sandboxes is a control plane. An MCP server running inside the sandbox is a tool surface for the agent. They are different products with the same name.

splits.heading: Dashboard-first and CLI-first
body: InstaBox, Lizard, Runtime, Blaxel and Morph document creating a machine from a dashboard. boxd and Boat are CLI-first: every guide starts with an install command, and the dashboard is a viewer for machines you already made. E2B and Vercel are SDK-first.
The practical test is whether the first machine can be created without a terminal. At InstaBox and Lizard it can. At boxd and Boat it cannot.

splits.heading: SSH is not universal
body: boxd, Boat and Sandboxer expose real SSH. Agent 37 tunnels SSH over a WebSocket, E2B proxies it, InstaBox routes it through a gateway, and Runtime carries it over its API. Lizard has no SSH protocol at all: its shell is over the provider's transport, so scp and port forwarding do not work. Vercel does not publish an SSH endpoint.

splits.heading: Two kinds of MCP
body: Sandboxer, Runtime, Lizard and Blaxel document a hosted MCP server that can create and drive sandboxes from Claude or ChatGPT. E2B has an MCP gateway inside the sandbox and a docs MCP, but a sandbox-management MCP is not established. Agent 37, InstaBox and boxd publish no control-plane MCP; Boat publishes a docs MCP only.
That distinction decides whether an assistant can start a machine for you or only read the manual.

watchFor: Whether the first machine can be created without a terminal.
Whether the API is REST or gRPC, and whether an SDK exists for your language.
Whether SSH is a real port, a tunnel, a gateway, or absent.
Whether the MCP server manages sandboxes or runs inside one.
Whether there is a desktop you can watch and take over.
